messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Lab-on-a-Chip Integrated Aerosol Particle Sample Collection, Pre-Concentration, and Colorimetric Analysis (Quasi-Real-Time Cascade-Impactor-Coupled Sampling)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Aerosol Impaction Surface (collection surface of the electrowetting chip onto which airborne particles are impacted directly, representing deposited aerosol constituents such as sulfate, nitrate, and ammonium)
  - Ultra-Pure Solvent (micro-droplet digitally directed across the impaction surface to wash and dissolve aerosol constituents)
  - Colorimetric Reagent (reagent that reacts with the extracted aerosol constituents to produce colored complexes for LED/photodiode absorbance detection)

STEPS:
1. Particle collection: Impact airborne aerosol particles directly onto the exposed collection surface of the electrowetting chip during a brief collection phase, with the air stream uninterrupted.
2. Extraction/washing: Interrupt the air stream, dispense a micro-droplet of ultra-pure solvent, and digitally scan/actuate it across the impaction surface (approx. 1 min sampling time) to dissolve and pre-concentrate the aerosol constituents into the droplet.
3. Reagent merge and mix: Dispense a colorimetric reagent droplet, merge it with the extraction droplet by applying voltages to the appropriate electrodes, and mix by shuttling the merged droplet across electrodes for approximately 5 seconds at an actuation voltage of about 50 V to form a colored reaction product.
4. Detection: Measure the absorbance of the colored complex at the target wavelength at room temperature using the on-chip LED (light emitting diode)/photodiode setup.
5. Disposal and cycle repeat: Dispose of the analyzed droplet; repeat the collection-extraction-mix-detect cycle so that sampling can continue in quasi-real time.

INTERPRETATION: Successful integrated sample collection and analysis is confirmed by achieving a time resolution of 1 minute per measurement (roughly two orders of magnitude faster than conventional manual cascade impactor methods), with the very small extraction-droplet volume producing a relatively concentrated solution that allows detection limits in air on the order of tens of ng/m3 (attogram-level analyte mass), supporting quasi real-time, fully automated on-chip quantification of major inorganic aerosol constituents (sulfate, nitrate, ammonium) as well as future extension to airborne bioagent detection.

module fluorescence

manifest Aerosol_Impaction_Surface
manifest Ultra_Pure_Solvent
manifest Colorimetric_Reagent

instructions:

repeat 3 times {

    // --- sample collection: scanning droplet washes impaction surface, dissolving analyte ---
    surface = dispense Aerosol_Impaction_Surface
    solvent = dispense 1 units of Ultra_Pure_Solvent
    extract = mix solvent with surface for 60s

    // --- reagent mixing: merge with colorimetric reagent to form colored complex ---
    reagent = dispense 1 units of Colorimetric_Reagent
    reaction = mix extract with reagent for 5s

    // --- detection: LED/photodiode absorbance readout of colored reaction product ---
    absorbance = detect fluorescence on reaction for 30s

    dispose reaction
}

sources.title: Integrated chemical/biochemical sample collection, pre-concentration, and analysis on a digital microfluidic lab-on-a-chip platform

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code represents the paper's quasi-real-time aerosol sampling cycle (Section 2.2 Sample Collection and Concentration, Section 2.3 Collection Surface-LoC Interface, and Section 3.1 Attogram Particle Detection Air Sampling), combining the scanning-droplet extraction/wash step, colorimetric reagent merge/mix step, and LED/photodiode absorbance detection step into a single repeatable cycle. Because BioScript has no primitive for a persistent physical impaction substrate (the collection surface itself remains fixed on-chip across cycles while droplets are scanned over it, per Figs. 3-5), the surface is modeled by re-dispensing an 'Aerosol_Impaction_Surface' manifest at the start of each cycle rather than a single reused droplet handle, consistent with how other translated protocols model persistent solid substrates. The 5-second reagent-mixing duration and room-temperature detection follow the paper's description of glucose/colorimetric assay mixing (Section 2.3, '...mixed by shuttling it across electrodes for 5 seconds at an actuation voltage of about 50V'); the 60-second wash/extraction duration is an illustrative stand-in for the paper's reported ~1 minute sampling time (Section 3.1). 'detect fluorescence' is used as BioScript's sole detect primitive to stand in for the paper's actual LED/photodiode colorimetric absorbance measurement, not a literal fluorescence readout. The coplanar/wire-traction droplet-scanning mechanics (Section 2.2, Figs. 3-4), the air/oil interface droplet transport (Section 2.3, Fig. 6), the LOD-vs-sampling-time derivation (Equations 1-2), and the specific glucose-assay kinetics (Fig. 7) are device-mechanics, mathematical-derivation, or separate-demonstration content with no corresponding BioScript primitive and are not modeled; only the core collect-extract-mix-detect-repeat cycle is captured here.

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes the sampling cycle as generally repeatable for quasi-real-time monitoring but does not specify a fixed number of cycles; 3 is an illustrative repeat count chosen to demonstrate the repeat-cycle structure, not a literal reported value.

The paper's impaction surface is a single physical collection area on the chip exposed continuously to the aerosol stream between washes; BioScript has no persistent-substrate primitive, so a fresh 'dispense' models the surface being available for each new collection phase, analogous to how other translated protocols model re-usable solid substrates.

numeric_mismatches.note: 60s stands in for the paper's reported ~1 minute sampling/extraction time (Section 3.1); the paper does not specify this as a literal mix-operation duration since the physical scanning/collection mechanism (Figs. 3-5) has no direct BioScript equivalent.

numeric_mismatches.note: The 'fluorescence' detect primitive stands in for the paper's LED/photodiode colorimetric absorbance measurement; the 30s duration is illustrative since the paper does not report a specific detection integration time for the aerosol assay.
